info.title: Creasura Agentic OS Protocol (CAOP)
info.description: Lifecycle API for the Creasura Agentic OS Protocol v0.1. Every protected operation identifies the authenticated principal and workspace, is authorized server-side, and returns errors in the standard Error shape with a trace_id.

servers.description: Self-hosted runtime (e.g. on your Mac mini)

post.description: Records something the OS learned from an external source. Replaying the same source event with the same idempotency_key returns the existing observation with duplicate: true.
Resolves observations against known state. Retrieved facts and inferred interpretations are returned separately.
Creates a durable obligation or objective. A commitment cannot be completed solely because an agent claims it is complete.

get.description: Returns outstanding and recent commitments for the caller’s workspace.

post.description: Produces an execution plan. The planner may use an LLM; the runtime validates the plan against schemas, dependencies, and policy.
Starts an authorized execution of a plan. Execution is asynchronous; acceptance does not mean completion.

get.description: Returns the current state of an execution.

post.description: Submits output and evidence for verification. Moves a RUNNING execution to VERIFYING.

409.description: Invalid transition or state version conflict

post.description: Moves an execution between states. Invalid transitions are rejected with INVALID_TRANSITION; a stale expected_state yields STATE_VERSION_CONFLICT.

409.description: Invalid transition or state version conflict

post.description: Evaluates an execution result against criteria. The verdict lists every check performed and its kind.
Persists facts, evidence, and outcomes with optimistic concurrency on expected_state_version.

409.description: Invalid transition or state version conflict

post.description: Evaluates progress toward a goal. Recommended actions are proposals, not authorized actions.
Grants or denies a scoped, expiring authorization for a consequential action.

PrincipalRef.description: An authenticated principal: a person, a role, an agent, or a service account.

EntityRef.description: Identifier of any entity known to the OS, e.g. "property/14-oak-lane".

EvidenceRef.description: Identifier of a piece of evidence (an artifact, observation, or record) that supports a fact or outcome.

ArtifactRef.description: Identifier of a stored artifact such as a document or report.

Expression.description: A condition evaluated by the policy engine, e.g. "recipient.type == 'client'".

Criterion.description: A success criterion. "type" selects the evaluator; other members are evaluator-specific.

Constraint.description: A constraint on how a goal may be pursued.

AuthorizationPolicy.description: What a caller must hold to invoke a capability.

Goal.description: A desired outcome that persists beyond a single conversation.

WorkItem.description: A bounded unit of execution that advances a goal.

Fact.description: A durable, provenance-bearing statement in the OS state. Every material fact has a traceable source.

Capability.description: Something the OS can invoke to perform work.

enforcement.description: Advisory policies are instructions to a model. Enforced policies are checked by the runtime before an action executes.

CapabilityDescriptor.description: What an execution provider can do, independent of any one AI vendor.

CapabilityResult.description: The outcome of a capability invocation.

ExecutionState.description: Execution states. COMPLETED, CANCELLED, and EXPIRED are terminal. Invalid transitions are rejected.

ObservationCreate.description: Something the OS learned from an external source. Replaying the same source event must not create a duplicate.

ContextBundle.description: Resolved context. Retrieved facts and inferred interpretations are kept separate.

Commitment.description: A durable obligation. It cannot be marked completed solely because an agent claims it is complete.

Plan.description: A validated proposal. The runtime checks it against schemas, dependencies, and policy before execution.

ExecutionAccepted.description: Execution is asynchronous. Acceptance does not mean the work is complete.

Transition.description: Every accepted transition is persisted with an actor, timestamp, reason, and correlation ID.

Verification.description: A verdict must identify which checks were performed.

RecordCommit.description: A state mutation. A conflicting state version rejects the transaction or invokes a declared conflict policy.

Review.description: Recommendations are proposals, not authorized actions.

scope.description: What exactly is authorized, e.g. a document, amount, or recipient.

Approval.description: A scoped, expiring authorization for a consequential action.

event_type.description: e.g. observation.received, commitment.created, plan.approved, execution.started, execution.blocked, approval.requested, approval.granted, execution.completed, verification.failed, record.committed, goal.achieved

MetricNode.description: A node in a hierarchical KPI tree. Variance beyond thresholds triggers Understand or a Commitment.

ApprovalRoutingRule.description: Delegation of Authority routing for a policy.
